title: PostgreSQL regexp_match operator precedence should be equal to concat

labels.name: PRs (with tests!) welcome
labels.description: a fix or feature which is appropriate to be implemented by volunteers

body:
### Describe the bug

SQLAlchemy's `regexp_match` precedence is lower than `concat`.

### Optional link from https://docs.sqlalchemy.org which documents the behavior that is expected

_No response_

### SQLAlchemy Version in Use

1.4.47

### DBAPI (i.e. the database driver)

psycopg2

### Database Vendor and Major Version

PostgreSQL 14

### Python Version

3.10.6

### Operating system

macOS

### To Reproduce

```python
from sqlalchemy import (
    Column,
    Integer,
    MetaData,
    Table,
    Text,
    create_engine,
    insert,
    select,
)

# Uncomment to "fix"
# from sqlalchemy.sql.operators import _PRECEDENCE, concat_op, regexp_match_op
# _PRECEDENCE[regexp_match_op] = _PRECEDENCE[concat_op]

meta = MetaData()

foo = Table(
    'foo',
    meta,
    Column('id', Integer, primary_key=True),
    Column('name', Text),
)

engine = create_engine('postgresql:///precedenceissue', future=True, echo=True)

with engine.begin() as conn:
    meta.create_all(bind=conn)
    conn.execute(insert(foo).values(name='Alice'))

    stmt = select(foo.c.name.regexp_match(foo.c.name + '$'))
    result = conn.scalar(stmt)
    print(f'\nGot {result!r}, expected True\n')

    conn.rollback()
```


### Error

Output of above script

```
2023-04-06 19:06:59,675 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine select pg_catalog.version()
2023-04-06 19:06:59,677 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine [raw sql] {}
2023-04-06 19:06:59,678 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine select current_schema()
2023-04-06 19:06:59,678 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine [raw sql] {}
2023-04-06 19:06:59,679 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine show standard_conforming_strings
2023-04-06 19:06:59,680 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine [raw sql] {}
2023-04-06 19:06:59,681 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine BEGIN (implicit)
2023-04-06 19:06:59,682 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine select relname from pg_class c join pg_namespace n on n.oid=c.relnamespace where pg_catalog.pg_table_is_visible(c.oid) and relname=%(name)s
2023-04-06 19:06:59,682 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine [generated in 0.00036s] {'name': 'foo'}
2023-04-06 19:06:59,686 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine 
CREATE TABLE foo (
	id SERIAL NOT NULL, 
	name TEXT, 
	PRIMARY KEY (id)
)


2023-04-06 19:06:59,686 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine [no key 0.00017s] {}
2023-04-06 19:06:59,703 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine INSERT INTO foo (name) VALUES (%(name)s) RETURNING foo.id
2023-04-06 19:06:59,703 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine [generated in 0.00027s] {'name': 'Alice'}
2023-04-06 19:06:59,879 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine SELECT foo.name ~ foo.name || %(name_1)s AS anon_1 
FROM foo
2023-04-06 19:06:59,879 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine [generated in 0.00024s] {'name_1': '$'}

Got 'true$', expected True

2023-04-06 19:06:59,880 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine ROLLBACK
```

### Additional context

I'm aware of the `.self_group()` workaround.

Current precedence values:

https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/1aef8e75a69319469d3b447422b8cdee2a1cf894/lib/sqlalchemy/sql/operators.py#L1660

https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/1aef8e75a69319469d3b447422b8cdee2a1cf894/lib/sqlalchemy/sql/operators.py#L1664

PostgreSQL docs indicate that `||` and `~` are the same precedence, but SQLAlchemy has `~` lumped in with `LIKE` etc.:

Operator/Element | Associativity | Description
-- | -- | --
. | left | table/column name separator
:: | left | PostgreSQL-style typecast
[ ] | left | array element selection
\+ - | right | unary plus, unary minus
^ | left | exponentiation
\* / % | left | multiplication, division, modulo
\+ - | left | addition, subtraction
(any other operator) | left | all other native and user-defined operators
BETWEEN IN LIKE ILIKE SIMILAR |   | range containment, set membership, string matching
< > = <= >= <> |   | comparison operators
IS ISNULL NOTNULL |   | IS TRUE, IS FALSE, IS NULL, IS DISTINCT FROM, etc.
NOT | right | logical negation
AND | left | logical conjunction
OR | left | logical disjunction

Source: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-syntax-lexical.html#SQL-PRECEDENCE-TABLE

For additional context I've read through other precedence issues but those seemed to be around things like type coercion whereas this seems (?) relatively straightforward barring any other compatibility issues this would cause.
